stages.desc: A kernel as a string or a .c file. No headers needed for this one.

stages.title: Front end
stages.text:
export
function $saxpy(w %.1, s %.3, l %.5, l %.7) {
@start.1
	%.2 =l alloc4 4
	storew %.1, %.2
	%.4 =l alloc4 4
	stores %.3, %.4
	%.6 =l alloc8 8
	storel %.5, %.6
	%.8 =l alloc8 8
	storel %.7, %.8
	%.9 =l alloc4 4
@body.2
	storew 0, %.9
@for_cond.3
	%.10 =w loadw %.9
	%.11 =w loadw %.2
	%.12 =w csltw %.10, %.11
	jnz %.12, @for_body.4, @for_join.6
@for_body.4
	%.13 =s loads %.4
	%.14 =l loadl %.6
	%.15 =w loadw %.9
	%.16 =l extsw %.15
	%.17 =l mul %.16, 4
	%.18 =l add %.14, %.17
	%.19 =s loads %.18
	%.20 =l loadl %.8
	%.21 =w loadw %.9
	%.22 =l extsw %.21
	%.23 =l mul %.22, 4
	%.24 =l add %.20, %.23
	%.25 =s loads %.24
	%.26 =s fma %.13, %.19, %.25
	%.27 =l loadl %.8
	%.28 =w loadw %.9
	%.29 =l extsw %.28
	%.30 =l mul %.29, 4
	%.31 =l add %.27, %.30
	stores %.26, %.31
@for_cont.5
	%.32 =w loadw %.9
	%.33 =w add %.32, 1
	storew %.33, %.9
	jmp @for_cond.3
@for_join.6
	ret
}
stages.desc: cproc, ported to Python, parses and type-checks C11 and emits QBE IR: SSA-style instructions over 32/64-bit ints and floats.

stages.title: Loop optimizer
stages.desc: Locals become registers, x[i] and y[i] become pointers that step forward, and the loop is unrolled by 4 with a remainder loop, behind a trip-count check. a * x[i] + y[i] is one fused multiply-add.

stages.title: Backend
stages.text:
saxpy:
    hint #34
    stp x29, x30, [sp, -16]!
    mov x29, sp
    cmp w0, #0
    ble .L2
    mov w4, w0
    sub x3, x4, #1
    sxtw x5, w3
    cmp x3, x5
    beq .L5
.L2:
    mov x17, x1
    mov x1, x0
    mov x0, x17
    mov w3, #0
.L3:
    cmp w3, w1
    bge .L11
.L4:
    sxtw x4, w3
    lsl x4, x4, #2
    add x5, x0, x4
    ldr s1, [x5]
    add x4, x2, x4
    ldr s2, [x4]
    fmadd s1, s0, s1, s2
    str s1, [x4]
    add w3, w3, #1
    cmp w3, w1
    blt .L4
    b .L11
.L5:
    mov x0, x1
    and x1, x4, #18446744073709551612
    mov w3, #2
    lsl x1, x1, x3
    add x3, x0, x1
    cmp x4, #4
    bcc .L8
    mov x1, x0
.L7:
    ldr s1, [x1]
    ldp s3, s2, [x2]
    fmadd s1, s0, s1, s3
    str s1, [x2]
    ldr s1, [x1, 4]
    fmadd s1, s0, s1, s2
    str s1, [x2, 4]
    ldr s1, [x1, 8]
    ldp s3, s2, [x2, 8]
    fmadd s1, s0, s1, s3
    str s1, [x2, 8]
    ldr s1, [x1, 12]
    fmadd s1, s0, s1, s2
    str s1, [x2, 12]
    add x1, x1, #16
    add x2, x2, #16
    cmp x3, x1
    bne .L7
    b .L9
.L8:
    mov x1, x0
.L9:
    mov w3, #2
    lsl x3, x4, x3
    add x0, x0, x3
    cmp x0, x1
    beq .L11
.L10:
    ldr s1, [x1]
    ldr s2, [x2]
    fmadd s1, s0, s1, s2
    str s1, [x2]
    add x1, x1, #4
    add x2, x2, #4
    cmp x0, x1
    bne .L10
.L11:
    ldp x29, x30, [sp], 16
    ret
stages.desc: QBE, ported to Python and extended with arm64 addressing modes, fused multiply-add and load/store pairing, selects instructions and allocates registers.

stages.title: Encoder
stages.desc: cimo encodes machine code itself, with no assembler or linker: offset, the 4 bytes of each arm64 instruction, and the instruction. The same compiler emits WebAssembly for the browser.

stages.title: Executable memory
stages.text:
>>> import cimo, numpy as np
>>> k = cimo.compile(open("saxpy.c").read())
>>> k.saxpy                       # 284 bytes of arm64, mapped read+execute
<cimo kernel saxpy>
>>> x = np.ones(1000, np.float32); y = np.arange(1000, dtype=np.float32)
>>> k.saxpy(len(x), 2.0, x, y)    # a direct call through ctypes; y is updated in place
>>> y[:4]
array([2., 3., 4., 5.], dtype=float32)

# what happened: the encoded bytes were linked with the runtime parts they use,
# written to an anonymous mmap (RW), switched to RX with mprotect (W^X), the
# instruction cache flushed, and each function wrapped as a ctypes callable.
# In the browser the same module is WebAssembly, loaded into Pyodide's memory.
stages.desc: The code is mapped into the running Python process and called on numpy buffers in place. Compiled modules are cached by content hash.
